title: Continuous realization of heart objects has connected lisse strata
statement:
Fix the finite-field and coefficient datum $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k_0$ and $\Qlb=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ of [def-weil-finite-field-fiber]. Let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite subextension of $\Qlb$, with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $T$ be a separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the raw rationalized category $D^b_c(T,E)$ [def-weil-rationalization-karoubi], the common-finite-stage category $D^b_c(T,\Qlb)$ [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], and their standard pairs and constructible hearts [def-weil-constructible-standard-tstructure, def-weil-constructible-heart]. Let $J_T$ be the specified derived extension-of-scalars equivalence of [lem-weil-pbc-condensed-e-realization] to constructible complexes of modules over the continuous coefficient ring $E_T^c$, where $E_T^c(V)=C(|V|,E)$ on the small pro-etale site. The categories [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed] and [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete] used to define its rational source agree with the same completed ring sheaf and reductions. For every $F\in\Sh_c(T,E)$, $J_T(F)$ is concentrated in degree zero. There is a finite good stratification $T=\coprod_\alpha S_\alpha$ by reduced locally closed subschemes, where good means that the closure of each stratum is a union of strata, such that for $a_\alpha:S_\alpha\hookrightarrow T$ the canonical derived pullback [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] comparison is an isomorphism
$$J_{S_\alpha}(La_\alpha^*F)\cong a_\alpha^*J_T(F)\quad\text{in }D(\operatorname{Mod}(E^c_{S_\alpha})).$$
Both sides are lisse sheaves in degree zero: pro-etale locally finite free over $E^c_{S_\alpha}$. Each $S_\alpha$ has finitely many open connected components $C$, and every nonempty such $C$ has a $k$-rational point $x:s\to C$ and one finite rank $r_C\ge0$, constant on $C$. The empty scheme admits the empty stratification. The restrictions $La_\alpha^*F$ lie in the lisse rational heart of [lem-tw-lisse-rational-realization]; the displayed isomorphism uses its specified pullback comparison.

proof.text: A field is Noetherian. Apply the finite-type-over-Noetherian lemma to $T\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ and the finite-type dimension bound. Thus $T$ is Noetherian and finite dimensional, and $\ell$ is a unit in every local ring because it is nonzero in $k$. The integral stratified-perfect characterization identifies the two integral categories in the statement, including their completed coefficients and reductions. Its closure under cohomology and truncation ensures that the standard pairs in use are the same pairs of ambient integral degree bounds and their rationalizations.

source.place: Proposition 6.6.11 and Proposition 6.8.11(3); verification of the scheme and integral-category hypotheses

proof.text: Write $B_T=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_T$ and $A_T=B_T[1/\varpi]$, as in the current lisse-localization-restriction statement. The continuous-coefficients lemma identifies $B_T$ with the continuous integral coefficient sheaf and $A_T$ with $E_T^c$, canonically by finite quotient maps and localization. Thus the functor $J_T$ of the condensed realization is precisely the functor induced by $K\mapsto A_T\otimes^L_{B_T}K$, transported through that ring isomorphism. The lisse-localization-restriction lemma states exact scalar localization, its cohomology formula for every integer, and preservation of both localized standard halves for this raw rational functor. Since $F$ belongs to both halves, $M=J_T(F)$ has cohomology only in degree zero. This uses the two integral representatives allowed by the two halves, not an integral heart lattice or a lisse hypothesis on $F$. The condensed realization identifies its target with bounded complexes having stratified locally finite free cohomology over this same $E_T^c$. Hence $M=\mathcal H^0(M)[0]$ has a finite locally closed lisse partition. The strict-tower slice-limit clause of the changed lemma is not needed here.

source.place: Definitions 6.8.3, 6.8.6, 6.8.8 and Proposition 6.8.14(2): degree zero and the finite lisse partition

proof.text: Refine that finite partition by the Noetherian good-refinement lemma. Give every new locally closed subset $S$ its reduced induced structure: choose an open $U\subset T$ in which $S$ is closed and apply the reduced-induced-closed-subscheme lemma inside $U$. By the locally-closed-stratum lemma, each inclusion $a:S\hookrightarrow T$ so obtained is an immersion and $S$ is a separated finite-type $k$-scheme (composition of separated and of finite-type morphisms, $U$ being quasi-compact in the Noetherian $T$). The continuous coefficient restriction lemma identifies $a^{-1}E_T^c$ with $E_S^c$ for the immersion $a:S\hookrightarrow T$. Restricting a local basis of $M$ to the inverse-image charts therefore keeps a finite free basis. The good property concerns only the underlying subsets, so this choice of reduced structure preserves it.

source.place: Tag 09Y5, topology.tex, lemma-noetherian-partition-refined-by-stratification; reduced induced structure and §6.8 locally closed coefficient restriction

proof.text: For each $a:S\hookrightarrow T$, the integral pullback of the statement is the strict-tower completed pullback: the integral-pullback comparison lemma gives a natural isomorphism $\gamma_{a,K}:La^*K\cong La^*_{\mathrm{comp}}K$ for every integral representative $K$ of $F$ (derived complete by definition of the integral category, with $\ell$ invertible on $S,T$), matching the defining finite-reduction projections and $\mathcal O_E$-linear, hence passing to raw rationalizations. Through $\gamma_a$, the normalized continuous rational derived realization compares $J_S(La^*F)$ with $E_S^c\otimes^L_{a^{-1}E_T^c}a^{-1}M$. For a locally closed immersion it states that this is the exact ordinary inverse image $a^*M$; its scalar-extension formulas agree with the specified $J$. This proves the displayed comparison and puts both sides in degree zero, locally finite free. The lisse rational realization is essentially surjective onto finite locally free modules and fully faithful. Choose its lisse heart preimage $L$ of $a^*M$. Full faithfulness of the ambient $J_S$ lifts the sheaf isomorphism $J_S(La^*F)\cong J_S(L)$ and its inverse; faithfulness makes the composites identities. Thus $La^*F\cong L$ is in the lisse rational heart. The pullback comparison is the specified scalar-extension comparison of that lisse realization, since both send each pulled-back basis vector to the same basis vector.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.14(2), Remark 6.8.15 and the normalized lisse pullback comparison; no flatness assumption on arbitrary scalar maps

proof.text: Each stratum $S$ is Noetherian. The connected-component lemma gives finitely many open components $C$. Transfer its finite locally free continuous module to the pulled condensed coefficient model through the canonical coefficient-ring isomorphism. The stratified-lattice-rank lemma applies to that module and says that its rank loci are clopen and exhaust $S$, including rank zero. A connected nonempty $C$ meets exactly one such locus: two nonempty disjoint clopen parts would disconnect $C$. Its rank is consequently one finite integer $r_C\geq0$. The coefficient-ring isomorphism preserves finite free bases, so this is also the rank of both continuous modules in the displayed comparison.

source.place: Definition 6.8.3; Stacks Tags 04MF and 04ME; rank loci of the finite locally free coefficient module

proof.text: A nonempty component $C$ is quasi-compact, being closed in the Noetherian stratum, and is a finite-type $k$-scheme, being an open subscheme of it. Its underlying space is Kolmogorov: on an affine neighbourhood distinct primes are distinguished by a basic open; if one point lies outside that neighbourhood, the neighbourhood itself distinguishes them. The quasi-compact Kolmogorov closed-point lemma therefore gives a closed point $c$ of $C$. The closed-point residue-field lemma applies to $C\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, since $k$ is algebraically closed, and identifies $k\to\kappa(c)$ with an isomorphism. Composing its inverse on spectra with the canonical residue-field point yields a section $x:\operatorname{Spec}k\to C$. This uses no smoothness or irreducibility assumption. If $T$ is empty take the empty good stratification; every assertion about components is vacuous, and the degree-zero assertion already holds by Step 2.

No new nodes were delivered and the statement is unchanged. Only Step 2 changed from the prior head 54684fc: it now cites the continuous-coefficients immersion-restriction lemma to identify B_T[1/ϖ] with E_T^c. Steps 1-6 were checked against every cited statement. Step 1: Noetherian and finite-dimensional, ℓ invertible, the two integral categories are identified by the stratified-perfect characterization. Step 2: the heart realizes in degree 0 because the localized halves go to the ambient halves (lisse-localization-restriction), with no lattice assumed. Step 3: good refinement of a DCC space (09Y5). Step 4: lifting through full faithfulness plus essential surjectivity of the lisse realization. Step 5: finitely many open components, clopen rank loci (det-lem-stratified-lattice-rank), condensed≅continuous for totally disconnected E. Step 6: quasi-compact T0 component, closed point, κ(c)=k by Nullstellensatz, no smoothness. BS 6.8.14(2) was checked in the PDF. Empty, rank-0, nonreduced and singular cases are covered. Two citation faults (C1/C3) are fixed. (1) Step 3 asserted that the reduced strata are separated finite-type k-schemes, which J_S of the condensed realization requires, but had no node for separatedness (composition of separated morphisms). No DAG node gives it, so I added the statement-only unsplit node lem-dl-a1-locally-closed-stratum-separated-finite-type (Stacks 01KU, 01T3, 01T5, 01T6; Mathlib candidates IsSeparated.stableUnderComposition, isSeparated_of_mono, IsImmersion.comp) and cited it in Step 3.
